question_text: A 50-year-old man presents to an ophthalmologist with progressive decrease in his visual acuity over the last 6 months. Past medical history is significant for schizophrenia diagnosed in early adulthood which has been managed with an antipsychotic medication for the past 20 years. The ophthalmologist performs a slit lamp examination and notes discrete brown deposits on the corneal epithelium in both eyes.
